primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic kidney disease (stage 3 CKD with proteinuria)
nice_guideline_used: NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) with TA775 for SGLT2 inhibitors

medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management per NICE NG28; essential for glucose control

medications.medication: Acetaminophen 300 mg / Hydrocodone 5 mg oral tablet
medications.dose: 1 tablet every 6‑8 hours as needed for pain
medications.duration: As needed — review pain regimen annually
medications.nice_justification: Analgesia for chronic pain; no specific NICE CKD restriction

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to target BP <140/90 mmHg (or <130/80 mmHg if ACR ≥70 mg/mmol), max 10 mg daily
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration step
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria, slow CKD progression and control hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any change in eGFR
medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and reduce cardiovascular risk in diabetic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG203 (TA775) recommends SGLT2‑i for CKD with ACR ≥2.6 mg/mmol or eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 12 weeks then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk‑equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential additive hypotensive effect; ACE‑I may enhance insulin‑induced vasodilation leading to symptomatic hypotension, especially if hypoglycaemia occurs.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure and symptoms after starting Ramipril; adjust insulin dose if recurrent hypotension.

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased risk of hypoglycaemia when SGLT2‑i is added to insulin therapy.
interactions_checked.action: Reduce basal insulin dose by 10‑20% after initiating dapagliflozin and perform glucose self‑monitoring for 2‑4 weeks.

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure reading not provided – assumed not at target; will monitor and titrate Ramipril accordingly.
Serum potassium level not available – assumed ≤5.0 mmol/L; baseline potassium will be checked before ACE‑I initiation.
Liver function tests not provided – assumed normal; baseline LFTs will be obtained before starting atorvastatin.
Allergy status unknown – will verify no ACE‑I, statin, or SGLT2‑i allergy before prescribing.
Exact insulin dosing not documented – dose adjustments will be guided by glucose logs after dapagliflozin start.
treatment_summary: Initiate ACE‑I (ramipril), SGLT2‑i (dapagliflozin) and statin (atorvastatin) to address proteinuric diabetic kidney disease and high cardiovascular risk, while continuing insulin and analgesia. Monitor BP, renal function, potassium, lipids and glucose per NICE NG203, titrating ramipril to target and adjusting insulin to mitigate hypoglycaemia risk.
